chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
What (bird) comes from thirty farsakhs, so it is by guidance (instinct), and what was more than that, so it is by eating (training).

key_terms.الأكل: Food/eating, here referring to conditioning through food rewards used in training birds to return from long distances
key_terms.الهداية: Guidance, here referring to the innate homing instinct of carrier pigeons
key_terms.فرسخ: A unit of distance approximately equal to 4 km; 30 farsakhs ≈ 120 km

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on homing pigeons and their guidance instinct?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical ruling about carrier pigeons used for message delivery, drawing a distinction based on distance. Birds returning from within 30 farsakhs (approximately 120 km) do so through their natural homing instinct, while those trained to return from greater distances are conditioned through food rewards. This ruling has jurisprudential relevance to ownership and permissibility of using such birds.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘What (bird) comes to you from thirty Farsakhs (120 kilometers), so it is by guidance, and what was more than that, so it is by eating’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
That (bird) which comes back from a distance of thirty farsakh is because of guidance and from a distance of more than this is because of food.’”
